comment: Every weight is traceable in SCORING.md. Layer A items cite published sources; thresholds marked app_defined are operational choices, NOT literature-validated cutoffs. Layer C items are expert-opinion / lived-experience informed, Tier 4, UNVALIDATED.

comm_elevated.basis: Butler et al. 2007 COMM original cut score >=9; self-report instrument

documented_prior_diversion.basis: Original repo SAMHSA HISTORY_OF_DIVERSION (CRITICAL) + ML label weight 3; kept as a clinician-entered DOCUMENTED record item, reframed in pattern language

early_refill.basis: PDMP dispensing-pattern signal reviewed under CDC 2022 Rec 9; threshold app_defined

mme_escalation.basis: Dose trajectory reviewed under CDC 2022 Recs 5/7 follow-up; threshold app_defined

mme_ge_50.basis: CDC 2022 Rec 8 lists >=50 MME/day among factors for offering naloxone; signal only, NOT a cutoff (CDC cautions against hard MME thresholds)

mme_ge_90.basis: Higher-dose risk discussion in CDC 2022; zoning app_defined; NOT a cutoff

ort_high.basis: Webster & Webster 2005 ORT high band >=8; external validation inconsistent — see SCORING.md

layer_b.basis: AI chart review — a flag scores ONLY with a verbatim quote verified against the chart text. Method: verified generation. No published validation for this layer as implemented.

layer_c.basis: Expert-opinion / lived-experience informed — Tier 4, UNVALIDATED. Capped: Layer C alone can never produce the high zone (enforced in code).
